question.text: Shubham Family Trust has funded a ZCZP issuance by Bal Vikas Samiti on BSE-SSE. Post-listing, the Trust asks Ms. Priya Shah, SIA, for a 'reasoned opinion' on whether the NPO has complied with the full Chapter 9 disclosure stack. Which of the following SHOULD the SIA verify?

answer.text: All of: 91(C) 60-day non-financial and Oct-31 financial / governance packs; 91(D) materiality policy, KMP authorisation and 7-day event disclosures; 91(E) AIR covering 67% program spend, with SIA assessment; 91(F) quarterly utilisation statements with separate-bank-account reconciliation.

explanation.text: The Logic: A full Chapter-9 compliance opinion spans 91(C) periodic NPO disclosures, 91(D) material-event regime, 91(E) AIR with 67% coverage and SIA assessment, and 91(F) quarterly utilisation with separate account maintenance. Each slice tests a different facet of disclosure integrity. The Trap: Narrow options (A, B, D) miss the integrated nature of the disclosure stack. A single filing view fails the Trust's materiality question. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C compliance reviews take a similar holistic approach; XXIII tests that SSE-specific scope. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Scope the engagement as a 4-module compliance review (91C / 91D / 91E / 91F) with one working paper per module. The final opinion cites specific non-compliance findings by module - a structure the Trust can use at its investment-committee meeting.
